foot.note: Per marching day. Engels table 7 / ch.1: Macedonian army averaged ~15 mi (24 km)/day, fastest whole-army average 19.5 mi (31 km)/day. Van Creveld: 15 mi/day steady "since time immemorial", 18th-c. armies seldom >10 mi (16 km)/day for long. FM 101-10 (1941) march table: 12-15 mi/day for a division, 15-20 for smaller units. Dupuy (dupuyinstitute.org verities): opposed advance ~17 km/day Napoleonic, ~26 km/day 1973.

horse.note: FM 101-10 (1941) par. 38 march table: cavalry (animal elements) 35 mi (56 km)/day normal march, "under conditions requiring maneuver, these rates may be increased". Low 25 mi/day for mixed horse columns; high ~50 mi (80 km)/day forced cavalry marches (educated guess for steppe horse armies with remounts).

wagon.note: FM 101-10 (1941): horse-drawn artillery / pack 20 mi (32 km)/day. Low: Engels, ox carts 2 mph for 5 h/day = 10 mi (16 km). High: van Creveld, horse-drawn transport in 1914 "twenty-five miles per day being reckoned as a steady average" (40 km).

rail.note: FM 101-10 (1941) par. 40: military trains average 20 mph (480 km per 24 h continuous), allow 3 h to load and 3 h to unload. Low: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2nd_SS_Panzer_Division_Das_Reich, unopposed rail move of ~700 km "would have taken three or four days" (175-233 km/day for a whole division incl. loading).

motorized.note: Van Creveld (WWII ch.): truck companies at "the regulation 100 miles per day" (160 km). Low: 1967 campaign, no army "stands much chance of covering more than forty miles per day" (64 km). High: FM 101-10 (1941) march table, trucks/motorized units 175 mi (280 km)/day normal march.

mechanized.note: Van Creveld conclusion: tracked vehicles can do 15 mph but no army sustained 75 mi (120 km)/day "for more than a very few days". High: FM 101-10 (1941) light & medium tanks 150 mi (240 km)/day road march. Mid 100 km = sustained operational pace between these; low 40 km = 1967 ceiling (64) minus friction.

tracked_heavy.note: FM 101-10 (1941): tractor-drawn heavy artillery 40 mi (64 km)/day; tanks 150 mi/day road march. Heavy tracked formations are limited by track wear and fuel (Das Reich 1944 road march: "steel tracks of the tanks ... wore out", https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2nd_SS_Panzer_Division_Das_Reich). Mid 70 km composite, grade C.

air.note: Operational redeployment of an air unit per day incl. ground echelon. Spitfire ferry range 1,800 km, B-17 cruise 293 km/h, F-16 cruise 933 km/h (https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Supermarine_Spitfire, Boeing_B-17_Flying_Fortress, General_Dynamics_F-16_Fighting_Falcon). Mid = one ferry leg of ~1,000 km per day with support; grade C.

sea.note: Envelope of naval.speedKmDay: sail 90-270 km/day (Casson), oared 90 km/day (trireme 6 kn), steam 450 (Liberty ship 11 kn), modern up to ~900 (20 kn). Mid 250 km/day for a mixed pre-modern/modern lift.

water.note: Impassable to land formations (ENGINE.md section 5: water cells need sea lift). Placeholder 0.

clear.note: SPEC FOR THE ENGINE (movement.weatherOddsByZone). Replaces the single Berlin table (movement.weatherOdds) with one table per climate zone. Zones: A tropical, BW desert, BS steppe, C temperate, D cold/continental, E polar = Koppen-Geiger main groups with B split into BW and BS, C/D boundary at coldest month 0 C, as in Beck et al. 2018. Lookup: zone of a theater = the majority zone over its land cells in the Beck et al. 2018 present-day (1980-2016) Koppen-Geiger map at 0.5 deg (Beck_KG_V1_present_0p5.tif, 360 x 720, uint8; numeric codes per the legend.txt shipped in the archive; doi:10.1038/sdata.2018.214, data doi:10.6084/m9.figshare.6396959, CC BY 4.0; paper fetched at https://www.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/pmc/articles/PMC6207062/), collapsing symbols A* -> A, BW* -> BW, BS* -> BS, C* -> C, D* -> D, E* -> E. One table per theater because the engine rolls one weather per day for the whole theater (sim.ts). Fallback when the map is not available: zone C (equal to today's Berlin table). Categories: clear, rain, mud, snow, the same four as movement.weatherOdds and WEATHERS; seasons are LOCAL (seasonOf already shifts southern theaters by six months), so a table is indexed exactly like movement.weatherOdds[season]. Use .mid; mids of each season sum to 1 (the engine normalises anyway). Derivation derived:weather-from-normals (data/SOURCES.md): per season, snow = S/N, rain = (P/N) x (1 - snow), mud = k x rain, clear = 1 - rain - mud - snow, N = days in the season, P = days with precipitation >= 1 mm, S = snow days (cover where reported), k = mud/rain of the old Berlin table (spring 0.517, summer 0.167, autumn 0.6, winter 0.652; educated guess, so every mud leaf is grade D). mid = the zone's primary station, low/high = min/max over the zone's stations. Zone A. Primary Bangkok Metropolis WMO 48455 (Aw). Monthly Jan-Dec series used: Bangkok Metropolis 48455 (Aw, primary) P 1.9 1.9 3.4 5.4 12.4 13.4 14.1 15.6 18 14.4 3.8 1; Singapore Changi 48698 (Af) P 10.7 6.5 9.4 11.3 11.2 10.4 10.4 11.1 9.8 12 15.4 16.3; Darwin Airport 94120 (Aw, southern hemisphere, months shifted 6 to local seasons) P 19.6 18.2 16.8 7.6 1.7 0.2 0.1 0.2 1.5 5.5 10.1 15. P = days with precipitation >= 1 mm, WMO 1991-2020 normals (https://www.nodc.noaa.gov/archive/arc0216/0253808/1.1/data/0-data/ Region-2 Thailand, Region-5 Singapore and Australia CSV sheets, fetched). Snow 0: days with Tmin < 0 C are 0 in every month at Changi and Darwin (same sheets) and Bangkok's coldest monthly mean is 27.3 C. restDayFraction.note: Engels ch.2 n.66: army marched 15 mi/day "and halted for one day in seven" (1/7 = 0.143). Low 0.1 for forced campaigns, high 0.25 for heavy trains. Weather odds (movement.weatherOdds) source: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Berlin climate table, Dahlem 1961-1990 precipitation days >=1 mm (MAM 27, JJA 28, SON 27, DJF 30 days) and Brandenburg 1991-2020 snow-cover days >=1 cm (MAM 2.8, SON 1.4, DJF 20.1). rain = precip days / season days; snow = snow-cover days / season days; mud share is an educated guess (days after rain/thaw with saturated unpaved ground); clear = remainder.
